about: Sites whose terms or robots.txt limit what Octo may do with them (instafy-web-research, Link-only sites). Each site's "kind" says which rules apply. "no-agents": the terms bar AI agents, bots, scrapers or any automated access or collection. Every reader and browser refuses the site, every redirect hop that lands on it, and every wrapper's copy of it; Octo guides the person to it instead. "no-reuse": the terms bar copying or republishing its content but not reading it. Readers read it; Octo summarizes it in its own words, cites "seen <date> on <host>", links back, never copies reviews, photos or price lists, and keeps its content out of anything published or shared by public link. A site without a kind, or with an unknown one, is "no-agents"; when terms are unclear, choose "no-agents". "terms" records the evidence: the terms page's "url", the day it was "checked", a short "quote" of the deciding clause and an optional "note". Guided mode: "home" is the site's front page; "search" is an optional https link template on the site's own hosts whose "{name}" placeholders, each a whole path segment or a whole query value, are defined in "placeholders" (format "text", "date" as YYYY-MM-DD, or "count"); "deepLinks": false means the terms bar deep links, so the person gets the home page and what to type there, and the site has no "search". The bundled copy is the floor: a space's copy may add sites, wrappers and placeholders and may make a site stricter, never remove one or loosen it (where several entries match, the strictest kind wins); a copy that is not a list is ignored with a warning. Matching: "example.com" matches that host and any subdomain; "example.*" matches the label followed by one or two public-suffix labels of 2 or 3 letters (example.de, example.co.uk, www.example.com.au). Hosts are compared as a browser connects to them: any case, trailing dots, ports and user info ignored, international names in punycode. Wrappers are services that serve another site's pages at an address of their own (translators, caches, archives, reader and fetch proxies). A wrapper is never refused itself, but its copy of a listed site is that site. "embeds" says where its address writes the site: "subdomain" (example.com.proxy.test), "subdomain-dashes" (www-example-com.translate.goog, with "." written "-" and "-" written "--"), "path" (web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.example.com/) or "query" (.../search?q=cache:www.example.com). Add a site when its terms bar AI agents or automated copying, with the reason, its kind and the terms it rests on; robots.txt is checked on every plain read anyway. Add a wrapper when a service serves other sites' pages under its own address.

query.about: what to search for: a place, area, hotel or product

terms.quote: using automated assistants (including AI-powered assistants) to access the Platform without express permission

sites.name: Agoda
sites.why: terms bar AI agents and deep links

terms.quote: datamining, scraping, spidering, indexing, storing or rehosting the Content outside our Platform
terms.note: The page builds its text with JavaScript, so the clause was read from its search listing. The same terms bar deep links into the platform without prior written permission.

terms.quote: Do not use bots, crawlers, scrapers, or other automated means to access or collect data

sites.name: Amazon
sites.why: terms and robots.txt bar AI agents

terms.quote: any use of data mining, robots, or similar data gathering and extraction tools
terms.note: amazon.com answered 503 to a direct read, so the clause was read from a dated copy of the same page (14 Aug 2026). Its robots.txt disallows every page for named AI agents (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User and others).

terms.quote: Develop or use any application or automated technology, other than as approved by NIKE, to interact with the Services

sites.name: Expedia group
sites.why: terms bar automated access and deep links

terms.quote: access, monitor or copy any content on our Service using any robot, spider, scraper or other automated means
terms.note: expedia.com answered 429 to direct reads, so the clause (last revised 26 Mar 2026) was read from the page's search listing. Hotels.com's terms carry the same list and bar "deep link to any part of our Service".

sites.name: Trip.com
sites.why: terms allow private, non-commercial use only and bar deep links

terms.quote: WE ONLY PROVIDE OUR WEBSITE FOR DOMESTIC AND PRIVATE USE
terms.note: No clause names automated access either way, but use is private and non-commercial only, so an agent's reading is unclear and the site stays no-agents. Deep links are barred: "nor may you create a link to any part of our Website other than the home page". ctrip.com's own agreement was not found.

sites.name: Tripadvisor
sites.why: terms bar AI systems and deep links

terms.quote: any robot, spider, artificial intelligence (AI) system, or other automated device, process or means to access
terms.note: www.tripadvisor.com answered 403 to a direct read; this is Tripadvisor's own copy of its terms (effective 15 Jul 2025). They also bar: "deep-link to any portion of the Services for any purpose without our express written permission".

sites.name: Google search, Maps, Travel and Hotels
sites.why: terms bar automated access where robots.txt disallows it; Maps links are fine as links

terms.quote: using automated means to access content from any of our services in violation of the machine-readable instructions
terms.note: google.com's robots.txt disallows search, travel search and most Maps pages for every agent; the Maps terms also bar copying and bulk downloads.

sites.name: RunRepeat
sites.why: its lab data and reviews are sold under licence, not for reuse; reading is not barred

terms.quote: Our most basic license agreement start at €1,000 per year
terms.note: runrepeat.com's legal disclaimer and robots.txt set no rule against automated reading; its content is licensed, so it is summarized and linked, never copied.

wrappers.name: Google Translate's page proxy
wrappers.why: serves a site's pages at www-example-com.translate.goog

wrappers.name: archive.today
wrappers.why: serves copies at archive.ph/<time>/<address> and archive.ph/newest/<address>

wrappers.name: the Jina reader proxy
wrappers.why: serves a site's text at r.jina.ai/<address>

wrappers.name: 12ft.io
wrappers.why: serves a site's pages at 12ft.io/<address> and 12ft.io/proxy?q=<address>

wrappers.name: an open fetch proxy
wrappers.why: fetches any page and serves it at its own address, such as corsproxy.io/?url=<address> or api.allorigins.win/raw?url=<address>
